title: Arkret Account Current Results
description: Authenticated Station results installed by selector and revision, with no client state reducer. Family-specific values are generated from canonical cell projection contracts.

value_circle_metadata.description: Circle — an intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary with its own membership, history_access and optional independent MLS group. Parent Realm membership supplies only the current-membership intersection gate; history_access is never dynamically inherited.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

realm_id.description: Parent Realm. create-locked; Circle never re-binds to another Realm.

profile_ref.description: Optional create-locked Circle semantic profile discriminator. Ordinary Circles omit it. Profile-specific creation paths MUST persist their registered profile id. Agent Sidecar is a separate ak.schema.agent_sidecar.v1 object and MUST NOT be represented by this field.

directory_visibility.description: Who may see this Circle exists as a directory entry. 'members' means only Circle members see its title/display/member_ids. 'realm_members' exposes directory metadata only and does NOT grant event or history access.

join_rule.description: How an actor becomes a Circle member. 'public' lets any active parent-Realm member self-join; it does not make the Circle globally discoverable. 'knock' requires the application/approval flow. 'invite' requires Circle admin add or invite.

content_encryption_floor.description: Optional Circle-local content encryption floor. When omitted, the Circle inherits the parent Realm's content_encryption_floor. Effective floor = max(parent Realm content_encryption_floor, this field). May only tighten, never widen, the parent Realm floor, and the effective floor is a one-way ratchet: once e2ee_required has been accepted it MUST NOT be lowered back to allow_plaintext (reducer rejects with content_encryption_floor_downgrade). e2ee_required is only meaningful when encryption_profile='mls_rfc9420'; a Circle with encryption_profile='none' MUST keep allow_plaintext. See zh/models/circle.md §7.

metadata_encryption_floor.description: Optional Circle-local metadata encryption floor (binary, symmetric with content_encryption_floor: allow_plaintext | e2ee_required). When omitted, the Circle inherits parent Realm's metadata_encryption_floor. May only tighten, never widen, parent Realm floor; the effective floor is a one-way ratchet (reducer rejects a lowering write with metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade).

agent_participation.description: Optional wrapped five-bit Agent ceiling. When present every bit is explicit and may only tighten the parent Realm ceiling.

encryption_profile.description: Circle content encryption profile. create-locked. 'none' means plaintext delivery/query/projection isolation only and is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor allows plaintext. 'mls_rfc9420' means the Circle owns an independent MLS group and MUST NOT derive its keys from the Realm-default MLS group.

content_scheme.description: Create/Genesis-locked MLS content scheme. Required exactly for an MLS-backed Circle and immutable for the derived group lifetime.

mls_group_id.description: Reducer-derived base64url_no_pad(utf8(canonical CircleId)). Present only on the materialized MLS-backed Circle and forbidden in the actor-supplied create payload.

durability_policy.description: Create/Genesis-locked exporter durability policy. Required exactly for mls_exporter_aead_v1; absent otherwise.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional reference to an intra-Realm Circle that defines this Morph's effective scope. Omitted means Realm-default scope. The producer signs the corresponding Event.scope_ref; the receiver verifies scope_circle_id.realm_id == Morph.realm_id and exact equality between the derived scope and Event.scope_ref before materializing the object's immutable effective_scope.

schema_refs.description: Authoritative structural schema set for Morph fields. Reducers MUST validate fields against exactly these refs; morph_kind and facets are not a replacement for schema_refs. Generic before-to-after transition validation is not provided by JSON Schema.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a morph_metadata object. Required instead of plaintext metadata when the effective metadata_encryption_floor is e2ee_required.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a ContentBlock for Morph content.

actor_kind.description: Closed Actor classification. agent is reserved exclusively for a controller-provisioned Agent; Applet-created or Applet-hosted automation uses bot; Ghost Actor is provenance rather than an actor_kind and uses integration for an external account/integration mirror or bot for an external bot mirror. MUST NOT include device: a device is an endpoint rather than an Actor principal. actor_kind alone grants no authority; authorization still requires the normative DID, provisioning/registration, Grant and Constraint evidence. See zh/models/actor.md.

handle.description: Arkret canonical handle string: <localpart>:<domain>. The @ mention sigil is not part of the handle.

agent_slug.description: Projection hint for a controller-scoped selector slug backed by ak.schema.agent_selector_claim.v1. Only valid when actor_kind=agent under ak.profile.agent_provisioning.v1; it is not a global handle and MUST NOT be used for authorization, attribution, or Directory discovery. The mention input token @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> resolves to this actor's principal_id before persistence only after selector claim validation.

status.description: Public projection of the AccountStatusRecord lifecycle values defined in zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md §3. Implementations MAY hide or coarsen this field in projection views.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional intra-Realm Circle (models/circle.md) defining this Relation fact's effective scope, supplied in the submit payload. For confidential_discussion_of it points to the private Strand's Circle. For structural relations the resulting effective_scope MUST NOT be wider than the narrowest participating endpoint scope (circle.md §6.1). Sidecar context mappings are native sidecar.context cells, not Relation objects.

effective_scope.description: Read-only immutable effective scope of this Relation fact, materialized from the accepted Event.scope_ref after the receiver verifies it against scope_circle_id and endpoint pre-state (circle.md §6.1-§6.2). For structural relations it MUST NOT be wider than the narrowest participating endpoint scope. It remains immutable across any later scope rebind and MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied content payload (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed).

relation_kind.description: Relation semantic. The standard kind vocabulary (kind list, cardinality class, truth-source class, weak_semantic flag) is machine-indexed in artifacts/registry/relation-kind-registry.json; detailed dedupe/scope/conflict semantics in models/relation.md §3-§6. Cross-Realm constraint: structural relations 'contains' and 'belongs_to' MUST NOT cross Realm (resolved from_ref and to_ref MUST share the same realm_id); weak_semantic=true kinds per the registry MAY cross Realm subject to two-sided authorization. Stays a free string so extension profiles can add kinds; unregistered kinds are opaque edges (unknown_relation_kind), never container/visibility semantics.

rank.description: Top-level rank string for ordered relations (e.g. contains-list-strand position). Encoding follows conformance/encoding.md §9. Aligned with Space.rank so all rank-bearing canonical objects expose rank at the top level instead of fields.rank.

fields.description: Edge metadata. MUST NOT contain a 'rank' key — rank moved to the top level in v1 to align with Space.rank.

value_space_metadata.description: A Space is a structural grouping object inside a Realm. Boards, lists, swimlanes, calendar buckets, document outline groups, etc. are all Spaces. Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership/policy/E2EE group; its metadata may be placed in an existing Realm/Circle effective scope via scope_circle_id.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

realm_id.description: Immutable Realm of this Space and of resources structurally placed under it. Producers explicitly bind new resources to this Realm; scope and capability checks remain independent.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional Circle scope for this Space object's own metadata and scoped structural relation facts. Space still does not own a security boundary; it only places its metadata into an existing Circle scope. Omitted means Realm-default scope.

kind.description: Space kind. v1 standard kinds include 'space', 'project', 'folder', 'board', and 'list'. Profile-defined kinds (e.g., 'swimlane', 'calendar_bucket', 'page_group') MAY be added via Realm schema/profile and MUST be registered. Unknown kind MUST schema_violation.

rank.description: Fractional-index rank within parent. See encoding.md §9.

schema_refs.description: Optional schema/profile references that further constrain this Space's contained Strand types, fields, or position invariants.

fields.description: Space kind-specific fields. For kind=list, wip_limit is an integer 1..100000 and wip_limit_enforcement is required with enum warn|reject|require_review whenever wip_limit is present; these are the sole write-policy source and MUST NOT be read from View. For kind=board, view_id may identify a default presentation. MUST NOT contain a 'rank' key (rank is a top-level Space field; see relation.md §2 for the symmetric Relation constraint and forbidden-wire-fields.json `fields.rank/space_payload`).

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional reference to an intra-Realm Circle (see models/circle.md) that defines this Strand's effective scope. When set, ALL Strand tracks (synthesis, discussion, etc.) share that Circle's membership, history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and encryption_profile. When unset, the Strand lives in Realm-default scope. The producer signs the corresponding Event.scope_ref; the receiver verifies that the Circle belongs to this Realm and that the derived scope equals Event.scope_ref before materializing the object's immutable effective_scope. Rebinding scope_circle_id is forbidden by default (failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden). For 'wide synthesis + narrow discussion' scenarios use two Strands linked by a confidential_discussion_of Relation (circle.md §7.2).

schema_refs.description: Optional authoritative schema set for profile-defined metadata.fields subtrees. Unlike Morph, a plain Strand carries no profile subtree and omits this field entirely; when present it MUST list at least one profile schema id. The container self-schema ak.schema.strand.v1 MUST NOT appear here. Every listed profile schema and its metadata.fields namespace MUST co-occur in both directions: the ref without the subtree and the subtree without the ref are both schema_violation, evaluated on the post-patch object. Writers MUST also bind the same schema id in the Event requirements.schema[] so replay validates against the write-time schema instead of the object's current schema_refs.
schema_refs.$comment: Bidirectional co-presence for concrete profiles is enforced in allOf below; see zh/models/strand-and-message.md.

agent_participation.description: Optional wrapped five-bit Agent ceiling. When present every bit is explicit and may only tighten the enclosing Circle or Realm ceiling.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a strand_metadata object. Required instead of plaintext metadata when the effective metadata_encryption_floor is e2ee_required.

content.description: Strand description body. This is base Strand content and is independent of the synthesis and discussion tracks.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is the Strand description ContentBlock. Exclusive with content.

tracks.description: Active Strand collaboration surfaces, keyed by an active name in track-name-registry.json. The synthesis entry may carry its own content / encrypted_content; the discussion entry configures a Message timeline and may not carry either field. Tracks do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE: the entire Strand shares a single effective scope determined by Strand.scope_circle_id (see models/circle.md). At most one track entry may explicitly set is_primary=true; when none does, the reducer derives the primary track by the deterministic rules in models/strand-and-message.md §4.5. The map MUST contain at least one entry; propertyNames fails closed for names outside the registry-backed TrackName enum.

visibility.description: View sharing visibility. Private views are actor-private account data; shared views are canonical Realm objects.

state.description: Required View lifecycle state. Shared View removal is an ak.view.update patch to tombstoned; tombstoned is terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the ak.view.update that transitioned state to tombstoned. Actor-supplied values MUST be rejected.

entry.description: The complete entry MUST occupy at most 7340032 RFC 8785 UTF-8 bytes; this semantic byte bound is independent of JSON Schema structural validation and request coverage.
